A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scaling study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAC, BRO, and PQL experiments across 12 tasks, empirical scaling fits, hyperparameter sweeps, and critical-batch-size analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds diagnostic comparisons and quantitative summaries in its appendices.

M1.justification: The hyperparameter-fitting workflow, power-law models, resource-allocation procedure, and SAC/BRO/PQL implementations remain unchanged. Gaussian smoothing is introduced as a comparison, not adopted into the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven DeepMind Control tasks, four OpenAI Gym tasks, and IsaacGym Franka-Push task listed in Table 1. The additional plots reuse retained task coverage.

E2.justification: New Figure 8 compares Gaussian smoothing against the workflow's isotonic preprocessing on two training curves. The existing constant-hyperparameter comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added smoothing comparison specifies a Gaussian parameter of sigma = 3, and Table 5 introduces percentage extrapolation-error reporting. Existing model sizes, hyperparameter grids, and extrapolation holdout rules are retained.

E4.justification: New Figure 8 examines preprocessing behavior on cartpole-swingup and cheetah-run, comparing isotonic and Gaussian smoothing. Figure 9 supplies empirical-point comparisons across return targets. The critical-batch-size analysis is retained, moving from Appendix E to F.

E5.justification: Figures 1 and 6 add shaded bands around fitted curves, although their construction and confidence level are unspecified. The reported 10 DMC, 8 OpenAI Gym, and 5 IsaacGym seeds and 100-bootstrap procedure remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New Tables 4–5 report correlations of 0.04, -0.40, and -0.46 and extrapolation errors of 7.8% toward larger compute and 10.6% toward larger data. Additional fits and IsaacGym predictions are supplied. Figure 6's left/middle axis multiplier changes from 10^4 to 10^3 without explanation; this is not demonstrated performance improvement. The principal scaling trends and existing fitted coefficients remain.

T1.justification: The resource-optimization problems, scaling equations, Appendix A derivations, and fitting mathematics are retained. Shortening the expectation notation in Equation 2.1 does not establish a substantive mathematical change.

C1.justification: The three central scaling contributions remain unchanged. However, v2 removes the conclusion's explicit first-demonstration claim and narrows the related-work novelty wording to studying predictability.

C2.justification: The explanations involving overfitting, plasticity loss, and hyperparameter relationships remain unchanged, as do the four substantive limitations in Section 7. The added diagnostics do not revise these interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies J = 800 for Figure 1's left panels. New Tables 10–11 explicitly list predicted Franka-Push batch sizes and learning rates across UTD values. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to the underlying experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Springenberg et al. on offline scaling, Lee et al.'s SimBa, Sokar et al., and Xu et al., and refines its novelty positioning around predictability. Other publication-year updates and duplicate-reference consolidation concern retained works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose cuts, shortens headings, reorders figure explanations in Appendix B, and adds an Impact Statement and an additional-results appendix heading. The main section sequence and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column conference formatting, relocating Figure 1 and resizing or repositioning numerous figures and boxes. Figures 1 and 6 are redrawn with bands; two appendix figures and four tables are added, while retained displays are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added quantitative diagnostics, smoothing comparison, and IsaacGym settings improve inspectability. However, Figure 6 introduces an unexplained tenfold change in reported data magnitudes, and the new bands and percentage-error calculation lack definitions. Because resource prediction is central to the paper, the PDFs do not establish whether these changes yield a reliable net quality improvement.
